lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use multi-carpellate ovary/berry architecture to separate core pokeweed from the modern Petiveriaceae split.

project_scope.note: The project follows current family placement: Phytolacca in Phytolaccaceae; Rivina is treated separately in Petiveriaceae.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Find the raceme of small apetalous flowers and inspect the ovary: Phytolacca uses several carpels, producing a distinctly lobed berry with multiple seeds.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Robust herbs, shrubs or trees depending on genus; leaves simple, alternate and without stipules.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually small, radial, in racemes/spikes/panicles; petals absent; perianth typically of 4–5 sepals/tepals. Stamens may be numerous.
family_diagnostics.fruit: In Phytolacca, multiple carpels develop into a fleshy multi-lobed berry containing several seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: For the local project: big pokeweed raceme + no petals + multi-carpellate dark berry = Phytolaccaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: raceme → apetalous flower → multi-carpellate ovary → lobed berry → Petiveriaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: The easiest way to learn this family here is to follow pokeweed from its many-carpelled flower into the dark lobed berry.

steps.title: 1 · Read the raceme
steps.look_for: Many small flowers spaced along an elongated raceme.
steps.why_it_matters: This establishes the pokeweed architecture before fruit forms.

steps.title: 2 · Notice the missing petals
steps.look_for: A flower with a simple perianth of sepals/tepals and no separate petal whorl.
steps.why_it_matters: This connects it to nearby Caryophyllales while separating it from showier petaled families.

steps.title: 3 · Count the carpels in the fruit
steps.look_for: A visibly multi-lobed ovary/berry formed from several carpels rather than one.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the clean split from project Petiveriaceae/Rivina.

comparisons.title: Phytolaccaceae vs Petiveriaceae
comparisons.rule: Project Phytolacca has a multi-carpellate ovary and multi-seeded/lobed berry; Rivina in Petiveriaceae has a single carpel and a small one-seeded red berry.

comparisons.title: Phytolaccaceae vs Nyctaginaceae
comparisons.rule: Nyctaginaceae uses a petaloid perianth and anthocarp around one fruit; pokeweed has small apetalous raceme flowers and a fleshy multi-carpellate berry.

visual_lesson.caveat: Older family treatments sometimes lump Petiveriaceae into broad Phytolaccaceae. The learner follows current project/POWO family placement for the taxa present.

genera.fast_cue: robust raceme + apetalous flowers + multi-carpellate dark lobed berry

visual_targets.annotation_goal: multi-carpellate dark berry vs small single-carpel red berry
